content.text: {"answers": [{"question_id": "Q1", "question": "What event or condition triggers the scheduling of a vendor meeting — is it a recurring calendar event, a specific equipment issue, a contract milestone, or something else?", "answer": "The meeting is triggered by an incoming request for improvement or a documented summary of an equipment problem. These inputs prompt the process to begin, leading to agenda preparation and then scheduling. It is not described as a fixed recurring event or contract milestone."}, {"question_id": "Q2", "question": "Which roles from your organization are expected to attend the vendor meeting, and who has the authority to approve or commit to improvement actions discussed?", "answer": "The equipment engineer and a meeting organizer participate from the internal side, along with the vendor's representative. A manager holds the authority to commit to improvement actions by formally assigning responsibility and deadlines to those actions after the discussion concludes."}, {"question_id": "Q3", "question": "How is the meeting discussion captured — for example, are written notes taken during the meeting, is the session recorded, or is the summary produced from memory afterward?", "answer": "The meeting organizer captures decisions and unresolved questions during the meeting itself using written notes. These notes feed into a shared document repository. The summary is then distributed to participants afterward. No mention is made of audio or video recording."}, {"question_id": "Q4", "question": "At what point in the process are action items formally identified and assigned to owners — during the meeting itself, or during a separate post-meeting review step?", "answer": "Action items are formally assigned in a dedicated step that occurs after the meeting. The manager assigns each item an owner and a due date once the organizer has already documented the decisions and open questions from the discussion."}, {"question_id": "Q5", "question": "What tool or method is currently used to track action item progress after the meeting, and how are reminders or escalations handled when a deadline is approaching or missed?", "answer": "A dedicated action-item tracking tool is used to monitor progress, with each owner responsible for updating their items. Automated reminders and status monitoring are identified as an improvement opportunity, implying that current reminder and escalation handling is manual or inconsistent."}, {"question_id": "Q6", "question": "What does a successfully completed process look like — what specific condition or output signals that this workflow instance is finished?", "answer": "The process is considered complete when all assigned action items have been tracked to closure, each item has a clear owner and due date, a meeting summary has been distributed, and an updated improvement proposal reflecting the discussion outcomes has been produced."}]}
